slides.0.title: Industry and society
slides.0.subtitle: KWV, transformation, exports and bulk wine
slides.1.title: From KWV to a free market
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The role of KWV
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Formed in 1918; set industry policy and prices, restricted yields and imposed distillation quotas; by 1924 about 95% of vineyard owners were members
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Deregulation
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Quotas were scrapped in 1992; KWV became a private company on 1 December 1997
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Towards consumer wine
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Under 30% of the harvest became consumer wine in 1990; over 70% by 2003
slides.1.content: To discuss industry change, use the three-step frame: quota system → deregulation → quality and branding.
slides.2.title: Transformation and empowerment
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The 2007 transformation charter
slides.2.highlights.0.content: In 2007 SAWIC approved the Wine BEE Transformation Charter after nearly four years of consultation: large enterprises (turnover above R35 million) meet all seven scorecard elements, small ones (R5–35 million) four, and micro-enterprises below R5 million are exempt (almost 80% of wine grape farms)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Milestones of black participation
slides.2.highlights.1.content: New Beginnings in Paarl (1997) was the first winery with significant black involvement; Mont Rochelle (2001) became the first wholly black-owned winery
slides.2.content: The 2007 thresholds were the scheme of the time; for the present position check current WOSA, SAWIS and transformation data.
slides.3.title: 2024 exports
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Totals
slides.3.highlights.0.content: About US$562 million (+4%) and 306.2 million litres (roughly flat)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Packaged vs bulk
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Packaged US$430 million and 123.4 million litres (about 77% of value, 40% of volume); bulk US$132 million and 182.8 million litres (about 23% of value, 60% of volume)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Markets and categories
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The UK is the largest market (87.3 million litres); the Netherlands, Sweden and the UAE grew; sparkling +34%, Cap Classique +19%, bulk dry white −17%
slides.3.content: A structural feature of South African exports: bulk dominates volume while packaged wine carries the value; a starting point for discussing price tiers.
On what date did KWV become a private company?
